column1: # Controls. Each row changes ONE point of ONE extracted source, and both
# comparisons must then fail:
#   ruby    trace.rb must stop agreeing -- the mutated side no longer matches
#           the original Full state, or the independent model, or both.
#   kernel  the CORE object built from the mutated source must no longer
#           reproduce the cells the original produced.
# `stage` says which of the two applies. `both` is an extracted kernel, which
# has each. `ruby` is the MODEL, which has no kernel: those rows exist to show
# that the model is load-bearing rather than decorative, by breaking it in the
# two places the trace is built to notice -- a free list served oldest first,
# and a list a new thinker joins at the head.
# A control that passed would mean the comparison cannot see that part of the
# state, which is the only way a cell-for-cell check can be vacuous. The lane
# also asserts that each row changes exactly one occurrence and exactly one
# line, and that every extracted kernel has a control.
